newsitem.title: UK: N Sea crudes firmer, one Forties cargo cancelled.
newsitem.headline: N Sea crudes firmer, one Forties cargo cancelled.

text.p: North Sea markets firmed on Monday as sellers held off for higher levels amid limited June availability and improved refining margins, traders said.
A June 28-30 Forties cargo was cancelled as a result of the production problems on the field and traders said they expected the July programme to be very light in the first decade.

The July programme had been expected to be released on Tuesday but one equity holder said he did not expect the full programme until Wednesday as none of the equity holders had been given an idea of their July liftings yet.
"It won't be out tomorrow. No-one has had a verbal indication (of equity lifting) yet so that has to come first," he said.

A cargo of June 26-28 loading Brent was bought by a trader earlier at July Brent -53 cents. Talk that one million barrels of June 28-30 Brent sold at a staggering August Brent -55 cents was not confirmed but many thought this level closer to the real market.
"But it's ridiculous if two cargoes trade at a 30 cent (per barrel) difference in one day," one trader commented.

Brent intermonth spreads firmed on the back of talk and a slightly firmer outright price. Brent July/August moved up from early indications at -31/-26 to recent talk around -25 cents. Brent Aug/Sept gained a few cents to -18/-15 cents.
August Brent on the IPE traded at 1800 GMT up 10 cents at $17.86 a barrel.
Next weeks CFD's gained some 10 cents over the day to trade as high as August -50 cents while a cross week June 24-30 moved at August -45 cents.
Trade of other physical North Sea grades reflected a firming market with a July 5-7 Statfjord trading at dated Brent +15 cents followed by a July 7-9 loader at dated Brent +20 cents.
A cross month Oseberg moved at dated evens.
